judged_text: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) then silently skips, dropping every teammate's calendar. A collective booking whose organizer has no destinationCalendar proceeds without any of the teammates' destination calendars and without any error, so no teammate calendar receives the event — the multi-host behavior this PR introduces no-ops for exactly that configuration.

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists:
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null,
```
Then for COLLECTIVE team events it tries to add teammates’ destination calendars via optional chaining:
```ts
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, this push is skipped and all `teamDestinationCalendars` collected from `users.slice(1)` are dropped. That means the PR’s new “multi-destinationCalendar” behavior silently no-ops in the configuration where the organizer (and event type) lacks a destination calendar but teammates have one, which is exactly what the finding describes (at least the dropping-without-error part is directly verifiable from the diff).
